note: GOAL: run the g_k / Δ_in instrument (eval_online --measure-gk) across the LoRA-rank (capacity) axis on enwik9 — the LOW-transferability stream — to turn the AGGREGATE crossover that rate_curve1 established (enwik9 delta_pct DROPS as rank rises: 4.03/3.63/~2.9 for r16/32/64) into the prequential MICROSCOPE. Frozen config is IDENTICAL to rate_curve1, so static/online delta_pct in summary.csv must reproduce it exactly — a free regression check that --measure-gk perturbs nothing (already verified end-to-end: the archive is byte-identical with measurement on/off, round-trip lossless, NLL mirror exact). The rank axis is EXTENDED to 128 on purpose: enwik9's optimal capacity is small, so pushing rank UP is where online overfitting / negative transfer (g_k<0) should surface. Read each run with evaluation/gk_curve.py and watch three numbers vs rank: (1) harmful % (g_k<0), (2) mean g_k (Δbpb / rel%), (3) transfer efficiency g_k/Δ_in. Two outcomes with different stories: (a) g_k actually goes NEGATIVE on a growing fraction = variance-wins = online overfitting = the headline phenomenon (retune/gate has natural-data support); (b) g_k stays positive but shrinks while efficiency drops = capacity MISALLOCATION only, no active harm → push into the overfit regime via epochs_per_train (a follow-up grid). NOTE this is the LOW-transfer endpoint of the transferability axis; add pile_of_law_eurlex + beancounter to grid.data (as in rate_curve1) for the full transferability x capacity slice. train_interval=1 -> g_k measured per chunk (max boundaries). Compress-only; measure_gk records raw bits+bytes+tokens per boundary into result.json.results[online].gk for gk_curve. lora_alpha unset -> sweep sets alpha=2*r.
